paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Nineveh looked untouchable, and Nahum says the LORD of Hosts is against her anyway: "Behold, I am against you" (Nahum 3:5). Nineveh was a city of blood, full of lies and plunder, and Nahum says she was "never without prey" (Nahum 3:1). God sees what a nation does to people, and He does not let cruelty have the last word.

Now look at what Nineveh was leaning on. Thebes had water for a wall and four nations in her corner, and she still went into captivity (Nahum 3:8-10). Nahum says Nineveh's fortresses are like fig trees with the first ripe figs, and when shaken, the figs fall into the mouth of the eater (Nahum 3:12). So don't put your trust in walls, allies, or a big crowd of merchants. I once thought a junk drawer was a safe place to hide, and friend, SAFE it was not!

So here's what I'd bake into your heart. Nahum ends with "who has not experienced your constant cruelty?" (Nahum 3:19), and I think that line is heavy, because a lot of people had been hurt. For anyone who has been hurt by someone with power, this passage says the LORD notices. And for all of us, it's a reminder to trust the LORD more than anything we've built to protect ourselves.
